STEP 1 - Scene: A snack/dessert-style plate of fresh berries and fruit: whole and halved strawberries, raspberries, and one blackberry. No sauce, oil, or dressing is visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square plate, roughly 22 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 22 × 22 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm². Using a round-equivalent diameter of ~22 cm: 3.14 × 11² ≈ 380 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Whole strawberry (top center)
- Strawberry halves/slices (three pieces, right side)
- Raspberries (four or five, center and lower center)
- One blackberry (left)

STEP 4 - Area (of ~380 cm² vessel):
- Whole strawberry: ~5% (about 19 cm²)
- Strawberry slices (three pieces): ~11% (about 42 cm²)
- Raspberries (4–5 small): ~7% (about 27 cm²)
- Blackberry: ~1% (about 4 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 24%, which is plausible for a sparse arrangement.

STEP 5 - Volume (area × typical height):
- Whole strawberry: 19 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 48 ml
- Strawberry slices: 42 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 63 ml
- Raspberries: 27 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 32 ml
- Blackberry: 4 cm² × 1 cm ≈ 4 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (fruit bulk density 0.5–0.7 g/ml; use ~0.6):
- Whole strawberry: 48 × 0.6 ≈ 29 g
- Strawberry slices: 63 × 0.6 ≈ 38 g
- Raspberries: 32 × 0.6 ≈ 19 g
- Blackberry: 4 × 0.6 ≈ 2 g
Total ≈ 88 g

STEP 7 - Energy (kcal/100 g, raw fruit):
- Strawberry (whole and slices): 32 kcal/100 g → 29 + 38 = 67 g → ~21 kcal
- Raspberry: 52 kcal/100 g → 19 g → ~10 kcal
- Blackberry: 43 kcal/100 g → 2 g → ~1 kcal
Total ≈ 32 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A sparse plate with about a quarter of its area covered by a few berries, roughly 90 g and about 30–35 kcal, is plausible. Berries are low-energy, so this total is reasonable.
